papers.title: Selective laser melting: the use of metrology to assure process integrity
papers.abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) provides the capability to produce complex geometrical shapes and innovative weight reducing parts. Currently, however, there is a need to confirm that the parts being produced are acceptable because the process cannot be fully assured. This is a challenge to companies wishing to use parts constructed via this manufacturing process for safety-critical components.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注增材制造的过程完整性计量，而非生物医学植入物的力学性能或结构设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structure design, stress shielding, fatigue testing, surface roughness, or osseointegration; it is a general metrology study for SLM process assurance without biomedical context.

summary_zh.method: 采用计量学方法评估SLM过程

summary_en.motivation: There is a need to assure the integrity of selective laser melting (SLM) parts, especially for safety-critical applications, due to current limitations in process assurance.
summary_en.method: Metrology techniques are employed to assess and monitor the SLM process.

papers.title: Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification of Floor Responses for a Nuclear Reactor Building
papers.abstract: After the 2011 Fukushima accident, engineers of nuclear power plants are looking beyond the basic design requirements and ensuring that countermeasures are built in to avert possible nuclear accidents. In seismic probabilistic risk assessment (SPRA), uncertainties can be classified in two ways as aleatory uncertainties or epistemic uncertainties. To improve the reliability of SPRA, the difference in seismic response due to difference of building modelings related to epistemic uncertainty was focused on. Two modeling methods were used for a seismic response analysis: a three-dimensional finite-element model and a conventional sway-rocking stick model. Simulated input ground motions related to aleatory uncertainty were generated for the input waves. Then, the seismic floor response results of the various input ground motions of the two modeling methods were quantified. For the uncertainty quantification related to the different building modelings, a statistical analysis of the floor response results of the nuclear reactor building were further performed. Finally, for the quantification of the uncertainty in the fragility analysis for SPRA, the way to use of these results were discussed.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及核反应堆建筑的楼层响应不确定性量化，与生物力学植入物设计或FEA代理建模无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on seismic response of nuclear buildings, not on surrogate modeling for expensive FEA, constraint handling, or implant/biomechanics design.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高核电站地震概率风险评估中楼层响应的可靠性。
summary_zh.method: 使用三维有限元模型和摇摆杆模型进行地震响应分析，并统计量化不同建模方法导致的认知不确定性。
summary_zh.result: 量化了不同建模方法引起的楼层响应差异，并讨论了其在易损性分析中的应用。
summary_zh.validation: 通过模拟输入地震动和统计比较两种模型结果进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve the reliability of seismic probabilistic risk assessment by quantifying epistemic uncertainty in floor responses due to different building modeling approaches.
summary_en.method: Two modeling methods (3D finite element and sway-rocking stick model) were used to simulate seismic responses under various ground motions, and statistical analysis was performed to quantify epistemic uncertainty.
summary_en.result: The differences in floor response spectra between the two modeling methods were quantified, and the implications for fragility analysis were discussed.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through simulation case studies with multiple input ground motions and comparison of statistical outputs.
